'''Li Jiayang''' {{Post-nominals|list=[[Fellow of the Royal Society|ForMemRS]]}} ({{zh|c=李家洋}}; born 1956)<ref name=chinavitae/><ref name="royal" /> is a Chinese agronomist and geneticist. He is Vice Minister of [[Agriculture]] in China and President of the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences (CAAS). He is also Professor and [[Principal investigator]] at the Institute of Genetics and Development at the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences|Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS)]].<ref name=chinavitae>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150604151521/http://www.chinavitae.com/biography/Li_Jiayang|archivedate=2015-06-04|url=http://www.chinavitae.com/biography/Li_Jiayang|publisher=chinavitae.com|title=Li Jiayang 李家洋: Vice-President of the Chinese Academy of Sciences; Botanical Molecular Geneticist}}</ref><ref name=royal/><ref name=scopus>{{Scopus|id=8938386200}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | pmid = 25651972| pmc = 4327311| year = 2015| last1 = Huang| first1 = X| title = Genomic analysis of hybrid rice varieties reveals numerous superior alleles that contribute to heterosis| journal = Nature Communications| volume = 6| pages = 6258| last2 = Yang| first2 = S| last3 = Gong| first3 = J| last4 = Zhao| first4 = Y| last5 = Feng| first5 = Q| last6 = Gong| first6 = H| last7 = Li| first7 = W| last8 = Zhan| first8 = Q| last9 = Cheng| first9 = B| last10 = Xia| first10 = J| last11 = Chen| first11 = N| last12 = Hao| first12 = Z| last13 = Liu| first13 = K| last14 = Zhu| first14 = C| last15 = Huang| first15 = T| last16 = Zhao| first16 = Q| last17 = Zhang| first17 = L| last18 = Fan| first18 = D| last19 = Zhou| first19 = C| last20 = Lu| first20 = Y| last21 = Weng| first21 = Q| last22 = Wang| first22 = Z. ==Education==
Li was educated at [[Anhui Agricultural University]] in China where he was award a [[Bachelor's degree]] in [[Agronomy]] in 1982.<ref name=chinavitae/> He continued his education in the [[United States]] where he was awarded a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1991 from [[Brandeis University]] for his research into the [[enzyme]]s involved in the [[Dissimilatory sulfate reduction|reduction of sulfate]] ([[Sulfate adenylyltransferase|ATP sulfurylase]] and [[3'-Phosphoadenosine-5'-phosphosulfate|adenosine 5'-phosphosulfate]] [[sulfotransferase]]) in the single-celled organism ''[[Euglena]]''.<ref name=jphd>{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Jiayang|last=Li |title=Purification and properties of ATP sulfurylase and adenosine 5'-phosphosulfate sulfotransferase from Euglena |publisher=Brandeis University |date=1991 |oclc=24577153|id={{ProQuest|304019708}}}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Li was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society|Foreign Member of the Royal Society (ForMemRS)]] in 2015. His nomination reads:<ref name=royal>{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/fellowship/2015/jiayang-li/ |title = Professor Jiayang Li ForMemRS |archivedate=2015-05-02 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150502204435/https://royalsociety.org/people/fellowship/2015/jiayang-li/ |location=London|publisher=The Royal Society}}</ref>

{{blockquote|Professor Jiayang Li has made seminal contributions to establishing [[forward genetics]] approaches in [[rice]] and in using them to understand rice growth habit. He has identified and characterized key [[transcription factors]] and [[hormone|hormonal signals]] that determine rice architecture, and he has demonstrated that this fundamental knowledge can contribute to the development of improved [[List of rice varieties|rice varieties]] through [[Marker-assisted selection|marker assisted breeding]].}}

Li was also elected a Member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS) in 2001,<ref name=nas/> a Fellow of the [[TWAS|Third World Academy of Sciences (TWAS)]] in 2004, a Foreign Associate of the [[National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences (NAS)]] of the US in 2011, a Member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] in 2012, and a Foreign Member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO) in 2013. In both 2016 and 2019, he became a laureate of the [[Asian Scientist 100]] by the ''[[Asian Scientist]]''.
